Maya (Marketing): Kickoff — ops claim sculpting sprint. Need a tight battlecard fragment vs CloudX and Generic LLM APIs. Focus: latency predictability, cost transparency, private parity. Can we do 3 quick test hooks and one demo prompt? :thinking:
Raj (Field): Love this. Short, field-testable claims please. Customers ask about 'hidden egress / marshalling' costs.
Sam (Product): Quick thought: lead with deterministic SLOs + predictable throughput. Example snippet: `Up to 99.9% model availability with reserved pools` — but need legal to vet number.
Nina (Sales): Bring out the routing story too — 'auto-fallback to regional variants' wins against single-region cloud vendors. :thumbsup:
Elena (Research): Bench idea: 1) 95th pct latency at 512 tokens, 2) cost per 1k tokens with/without KV cache, 3) cold-start throughput. Can produce numbers by EOD if infra frees a slot.
Maya (Marketing): Great. Format for battlecard: one-liner claim, proof bullet (bench), field objection rebuttal, demo prompt. Keep each claim <= 20 words.
Sam (Product): Draft claim A (latency): "Predictable 95th-pct latency with reserved inference pools." Proof: bench + routing policy. Objection: 'What about spikes?' Rebuttal: automatic burst + fallback to cheaper variant.
Raj (Field): Love that. For cloud APIs, emphasize 'no model ownership' vs 'no predictable latency'. Avoid direct vendor names, use 'major cloud APIs' phrasing.
Nina (Sales): Quick callout: Procurement asks about data residency. Add one-liner: "Private deployments with customer-managed VPCs and KMS support." Short proof: compliance packages + audit logs.
Elena (Research): I'll attach a mini-table in my doc: test | metric | redwood | cloudX | generic-api. But for Slack keep it short.
Maya (Marketing): OK put drafts here. I'll stitch into a one-pager and mock a webinar slide. @Sam can you confirm the exact SLA language we can display?
Sam (Product): I'll ping Legal. Tentative safe phrase: "SLA-backed latency targets for Dedicated customers" until legal signs off.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: benchmark cluster spin-up at 18:30 UTC — job id `b-2023113` :robot_face:
Nina (Sales): Field request: include 2 quick demo prompts for SDRs to run — one for latenc y demo, one for cost demo. Keep prompts < 30 words.
Raj (Field): I'll curate the prompts. Also want a 1-liner objection script: "If they call price, ask about token-level observability and unit economics comparisons." :memo:
Maya (Marketing): Awesome team. Goal: ship a battlecard draft + 3 slide webinar hook by tomorrow 11:00 PT. Quick standup 9:30? :calendar:
Sam (Product): 9:30 works for me.
Elena (Research): Bench numbers will be posted here when ready.
Maya (Marketing): Thanks all — I'll open a PR in the docs repo after the 9:30 and tag everyone for review. :sparkles:
